source: Jeffrey Dodson's Greek Lexicon (public domain); frequencies counted in the SBLGNT

Αἰνών.d: Aenon; Eusebius and Jerome place this site 8 (Roman) miles south of Scythopolis near the Jordan.

Αὐγοῦστος.d: Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor, C. Iulius Octauianus, denoting sanctity (almost divinity).

Βάαλ.d: Baal, chief deity of the Phoenicians and other Semitic nations.

Βέροια.d: Berea, a town of the province Macedonia.

Βαβυλών.d: (a) Babylon, the ancient city on the Euphrates, to which the people of Jerusalem, etc., were transported, (b) hence allegorically of Rome, from the point of view of the Christian people.

Βαλάκ.d: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.

Βαλαάμ.d: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.

Βαράκ.d: Barak, one of the judges of Israel.

Βαραχίας.d: Barachiah; his identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zechariah killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War.

Βαρθολομαῖος.d: Bartholomew, surname of Nathanael, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

Βαριησοῦς.d: Bar-Jesus, the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus; he is also called Elymas.

Βαρναβᾶς.d: Barnabas, a Cypriote Jew, uncle of John Mark; his other name was Joseph.

Βαρσαββᾶς.d: Barsabbas, son of Sabbas, a surname of Joseph and Judas.

Βεελζεβούλ.d: Beelzebul, a name of Satan, the chief of evil spirits.

Βελιάρ.d: Belial, a demon, and in fact a name for Satan.

Βενιαμίν.d: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

Βερνίκη.d: Bernice, daughter of Agrippa I and Kypros, and sister of M. Julius Agrippa II.

Βηθανία.d: (a) Bethany, the home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, near Jerusalem, (b) Bethany, beyond Jordan.

Βηθεσδά.d: Bethesda, name of a pool in Jerusalem.

Βηθσαϊδά.d: Bethsaida, (a) a city of Galilee, (b) a city east of the Jordan.

Βηθφαγή.d: Bethphage, a village in the neighborhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.

Βιθυνία.d: Bithynia, a Roman province, north-west of Asia Minor and south-west of the Black Sea.

Βλάστος.d: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I.

Γάδ.d: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

Γάζα.d: Gaza, an old town in the south of Palestine, on the sea-coast.

Γάϊος.d: Gaius, (a) a Corinthian, (b) a Macedonian, (c) a citizen of Derbe, (d) an Ephesian.

Γαββαθα.d: Gabbatha, a sort of paved square, on which the procurator had his judgment seat.

Γαβριήλ.d: the angel Gabriel, a messenger of God.

Γαδαρηνός.d: Gadarene, belonging to Gadara (an important Hellenized town, one of the Decapolis, and south-east of the Sea of Galilee).

Γαλάτης.d: a Galatian (meaning any inhabitant of the Roman province Galatia).

Γαλατία.d: Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor, comprising the districts of Paphlagonia, Pontus Galaticus, Galatia (in the narrower sense, which some still think is intended in the NT), Phrygia Galatica, Lycaonia Galatica, Pisidia and Isaurica.

Γαλατικός.d: Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia.

Γαλιλαία.d: Galilee, a district towards the southern end of the Roman province Syria; the northern division of Palestine.

Γαλιλαῖος.d: a Galilean, an inhabitant of Galilee.

Γαλλίων.d: Gallio, Lucius Iunius Gallio, who received this name by adoption into another family, but was born brother of the philosopher Seneca and originally named L. Annaeus Nouatus; proconsul of the Roman province Achaia from spring A.D. 52 to spring 53.

Γαμαλιήλ.d: Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul.

Γεδεών.d: Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel.

Γεννησαρέτ.d: Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias, which was in consequence sometimes called the Lake of Gennesaret.

Γολγοθᾶ.d: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem.

Γόμορρα.d: Gomorrah, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea.

Γώγ.d: Gog, in Ezekiel a king of Magog, a land of the remote north; hence, in Revelation, of a people far remote from Palestine.

Δέρβη.d: Derbe, a town in Lycaonia and in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

Δίδυμος.d: the Twin; Didymus, the Greek name equivalent to Thomas.

Δαλμανουθά.d: Dalmanutha, a town or village near Magdala.

Δαλματία.d: Dalmatia, a province of the Roman Empire, east of the Adriatic, a later name for part of what was earlier called Illyricum.

Δαμασκηνός.d: a Damascene, an inhabitant of Damascus.

Δεκάπολις.d: Decapolis, meaning a group or district of ten cities (of the Greek type) in Palestine, mostly south-east of the Lake of Tiberias; the names and number vary in ancient authorities.

Δημᾶς.d: Demas, a helper of Paul in Rome.

Διάβολος.d: (adj. used often as a noun), slanderous; with the article: the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.

Διόσκουροι.d: the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, sons of Zeus and Leda, and patrons of sailors.

Δορκάς.d: Dorcas, the Greek name of Tabitha.

Δρούσιλλα.d: Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa I.

Εὐοδία.d: Euodia, or rather Euhodia, a Christian woman of Philippi.

Εὐφράτης.d: the Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria.

Εὔβουλος.d: Eubulus, a Christian with Paul in Rome.

Εὔτυχος.d: Eutychus, a young hearer of Paul at Troas.

Εὕα.d: Eve, the first woman; wife of first man Adam.

Ζάρα.d: Zerah, son of Judah and Tamar.

Ζαβουλών.d: Zebulon, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the twelve tribes.

Ζαχαρίας.d: Zechariah, (a) a priest referred to as a son of Jehoiada, (b) another priest, father of John the Baptist.

Ζεβεδαῖος.d: Zebedee, father of the apostles James and John.

Ζεύς.d: Zeus, the Greek god of the sky in all its manifestations, corresponding to the Roman Jupiter and to the leading god of the native Lycaonians.

Ζηλωτής.d: one who is eagerly devoted to a person or a thing, a zealot.

Ζοροβαβέλ.d: Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel (Salathiel) and father of Abiud and Rhesa.

Θάλασσα.d: (a) the sea, in contrast to the land, (b) a particular sea or lake, e.g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.

Θαδδαῖος.d: Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles.

Θαμάρ.d: Tamar, mother of Perez and Zerah by Judah, son of Jacob.

Θεσσαλονίκη.d: Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.

Θευδᾶς.d: Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C., otherwise unknown.

Θεόφιλος.d: Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank, to whom the Gospel and Acts are dedicated.

Θυάτειρα.d: Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia, in the Roman province Asia.

Θωμᾶς.d: Thomas, also called Didymus, one of the Twelve.

Κάϊν.d: (Hebrew), Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.

Καισάρεια.d: Two cities of Palestine: one in Galilee (Caesarea Philippi), the other on the coast of the Mediterranean.

Καλός.d: beautiful, as an outward sign of the inward good, noble, honorable character; good, worthy, honorable, noble, and seen to be so.

Κανδάκη.d: Candace, a proper name; the Candace, a dynastic name for queens of the Ethiopians in Abyssinia.

Καππαδοκία.d: Cappadocia, a large Roman province in the central eastern part of Asia Minor.

Καῖσαρ.d: Caesar, a surname of the gens Iulia, which became practically synonymous with the Emperor for the time being; in the Gospels it always refers to Tiberias.

Κεγχρεαί.d: Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.

Κηφᾶς.d: Cephas (Aramaic for rock), the new name given to Simon Peter, the apostle.

Κιλικία.d: Cilicia, a Roman province between the Taurus range of mountains and the coast in the south-east corner of Asia Minor, linked up with the province of Syria.

Κλήμης.d: Clement, a fellow-worker of Paul in Rome.

Κλαυδία.d: Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome; probably a freedwoman of the imperial household.

Κλαύδιος.d: (a) Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors, Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, who ruled A.D. 41-54, (b) Claudius Lysias, a tribune at Jerusalem.

Κλεοπᾶς.d: Cleopas, one of the two companions of the risen Jesus from Jerusalem to Emmaus.

Κλωπᾶς.d: Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross.

Κνίδος.d: Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria (south-west Asia Minor) near the island of Cos.

Κολοσσαί.d: Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia, in the Lycus valley, near Laodicea and Hierapolis.

Κορβᾶν.d: a gift, offering, anything consecrated to God.

Κορνήλιος.d: Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army, stationed at Caesarea.

Κούαρτος.d: Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian.

Κρής.d: a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete.

Κρήσκης.d: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of Paul.

Κρίσπος.d: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by Paul.

Κυρήνη.d: Cyrene, a district west of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast, forming with Crete a Roman province.

Κυρήνιος.d: Cyrenius or Quirinius, governor of Syria.

Κωσάμ.d: Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addi.

Κόρινθος.d: Corinth, in north-east Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.

Κώς.d: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, south-west of Asia Minor.

Λάζαρος.d: Lazarus, Eliezer, (a) the beggar, (b) the brother of Martha and Mary, of Bethany.

Λάμεχ.d: (Hebrew), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.

Λαοδίκεια.d: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.

Λαοδικεύς.d: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.

Λασαία.d: Lasea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the south coast.

Λευί.d: (Hebrew), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, (b) another ancestor of Jesus, (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, (d) son of Alphaeus, and called Matthew, a revenue officer and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

Λευίς.d: (Hebrew), Levi, son of Alphaeus, the publican.

Λευίτης.d: a Levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence: a priest's assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.

Λευιτικός.d: belonging to the tribe of Levi; Levitical.

Λιβερτῖνος.d: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves; a synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.

Λουκᾶς.d: Lucas, Luke, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.

Λούκιος.d: Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, by some identified with the evangelist Luke, (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a).

Λυδία.d: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.

Λυκία.d: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.

Λυκαονία.d: Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities of Derbe and Lystra.

Λυσίας.d: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.

Λύδδα.d: Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day's journey of Jerusalem.

Λύστρα.d: Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

Μάλχος.d: Malchus, a servant of the high-priest at Jerusalem.

Μάρθα.d: Martha, sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.

Μίλητος.d: Miletus, a city on the coast of the Roman province Asia.

Μαγώγ.d: (Hebrew), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in the Old Testament, probably the Scythians; hence: used in apocalyptic literature.

Μαδιάμ.d: (Hebrew), Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.

Μαθουσαλά.d: (Hebrew) Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech.

Μακεδονία.d: (Hebrew), Macedonia, a Roman province north of Achaia (Greece).

Μακεδών.d: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.

Μαλελεήλ.d: Mahalaleel or Maleleel, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Μαναήν.d: (Graecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas' court.

Μανασσῆς.d: (Hebrew), Manasseh, (a) son of Joseph, founder of a tribe of Israel, (b) son of Hezekiah and father of Amon (Amos).

Μαρία.d: Mary, Miriam, (a) the mother of Jesus, (b) of Magdala, (c) sister of Martha and Lazarus, (d) wife of Cleopas, (e) mother of John Mark, (f) a Christian woman in Rome.

Μαριάμ.d: Mary, Miriam, (a) the mother of Jesus, (b) of Magdala, (c) sister of Martha and Lazarus, (d) wife of Cleopas, (e) mother of John Mark, (f) a Christian woman in Rome.

Μελχί.d: Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Μελχισέδεκ.d: Melchizedek, king and priest of Salem.

Μεσοποταμία.d: Mesopotamia, the Country between the (two) Rivers, i.e. the Euphrates and the Tigris.

Μιτυλήνη.d: Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos in the northern Aegean sea.

Μνάσων.d: Mnason, an early Christian, native of Cyprus, resident at a place between Caesarea and Jerusalem.

Μολόχ.d: Moloch, a god worshipped by several Semitic peoples.

Μυσία.d: Mysia, a country in the north-west of the Roman province Asia (and of Asia Minor).

Μωϋσῆς.d: Moses; met: the books of Moses, the Pentateuch.

Μύρα.d: Myra, a port in Lycia, south-west Asia Minor.

Μᾶρκος.d: Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary, nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Paul, and Peter.

Μῆδος.d: a Mede, a Median, from east of Assyria.

Ναΐν.d: Nain, a city south-west of the Sea of Galilee.

Ναασσών.d: Nahshon, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Ναγγαί.d: Naggai, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Ναζαρέθ.d: Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.

Ναζαρέτ.d: Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.

Ναζωραῖος.d: a Nazarene, an inhabitant of Nazareth.

Ναθαναήλ.d: Nathanael, of Cana in Galilee, an early disciple, probably to be identified with Bartholomew.

Ναχώρ.d: Nahor, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Νικολαΐτης.d: a Nicolaitan, possibly a follower of Nicolaus (a heretic at Ephesus).

Νικόδημος.d: Nicodemus, a member of the Sanhedrin.

Νινευίτης.d: a Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh, a city on the Tigris in Assyria.

Οὐρίας.d: Uriah, husband of Bathsheba the mother of Solomon.

Οὐρβανός.d: Urbanus, a Christian in Rome, fellow-worker of Paul.

Πάρθος.d: a Parthian, an inhabitant of the country beyond the eastern boundary of the Roman Empire between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf.

Πάταρα.d: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.

Πάτμος.d: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Ephesus.

Πάφος.d: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.

Πέργαμος.d: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia.

Πέργη.d: Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia.

Παμφυλία.d: Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.

Παρμενᾶς.d: Parmenas, one of the original seven deacons at Jerusalem.

Περσίς.d: Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome.

Πισιδία.d: Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor, being the south-western part of the Roman province Galatia.

Ποτίολοι.d: Puteoli, the great harbor for traffic with Alexandria on the Bay of Naples.

Πούδης.d: Pudens, a Christian man in Rome.

Πρίσκα.d: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.

Πρίσκιλλα.d: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.

Πρόχορος.d: Prochorus, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.

Πτολεμαΐς.d: Ptolemais, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.

Πόλις.d: a city, the inhabitants of a city.

Πόντος.d: Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor, bordering on the Black Sea, governed along with Bithynia.

Πόρκιος.d: Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus.

Σάμος.d: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.

Σάρδεις.d: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.

Σάρεπτα.d: Zarephath, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.

Σέργιος.d: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.

Σίλας.d: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.

Σαδδουκαῖος.d: a Sadducee, a member of the aristocratic party among the Jews, from whom the high-priests were almost invariably chosen.

Σαλά.d: Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus.

Σαλαμίς.d: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.

Σαλμών.d: Salmon, son of Nahshon and father of Boaz.

Σαλμώνη.d: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.

Σαλώμη.d: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the apostles.

Σαμάρεια.d: Samaria, a small district of Palestine, bounded by Galilee on the north, and by Judaea on the south, and taking its name from the city of Samaria, the ancient capital of the kingdom of (northern) Israel.

Σαμοθρᾴκη.d: Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace.

Σαμψών.d: Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.

Σαούλ.d: Saul, (a) the first king of Israel, (b) the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles.

Σεβαστός.d: (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), venerated, august, a title of the Roman emperors; hence secondarily: Augustan, imperial.

Σελεύκεια.d: Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbor of Syrian Antioch.

Σιδών.d: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia.

Σιλουανός.d: Silvanus, a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.

Σιλωάμ.d: Siloam, a spring within the walls, in the south-east corner of Jerusalem.

Σιλᾶς.d: Silas, a pet-form of the name "Silvanus"; a Roman citizen and a helper of Paul.

Σιών.d: Zion, the hill; used for Jerusalem or heaven.

Σκύθης.d: a Scythian, as typical of the uncivilized.

Σμύρνα.d: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.

Σολομών.d: Solomon, son of David King of Israel, and Bathsheba.

Σολομῶν.d: Solomon, son of David King of Israel, and Bathsheba.

Σουσάννα.d: Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus.

Σπανία.d: Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country of the name.

Στάχυς.d: Stachys, a Christian man at Rome.

Στέφανος.d: Stephen, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.

Συντύχη.d: Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi.

Συρία.d: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia.

Συροφοινίκισσα.d: Syrophoenician, i.e. Phoenician (of Syria, in contrast to Carthage and its territory in North Africa).

Σωσθένης.d: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth.

Σύρτις.d: Syrtis, a quicksand off the coast of North Africa.

Τέρτιος.d: Tertius, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation.

Τέρτυλλος.d: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea.

Τίμων.d: Timon, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.

Τίτος.d: Titus, a Greek Christian, helper of Paul, perhaps also brother of Luke.

Ταρσός.d: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.

Τιβέριος.d: Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).

Τιβεριάς.d: Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.

Τιμαῖος.d: Timaeus, father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus.

Τιμόθεος.d: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul.

Τραχωνῖτις.d: Trachonitis, the north-east of the territory beyond Jordan.

Τρυφῶσα.d: Tryphosa, a Christian woman in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.

Τρόφιμος.d: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.

Τρύφαινα.d: Tryphaena, a Christian woman in Rome.

Τρῳάς.d: Troas, a harbor city of Mysia.

Τυχικός.d: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.

Τύραννος.d: Tyrannus, an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.

Τύριος.d: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.

Τύρος.d: Tyre, an ancient city, the capital of Phoenicia.

Φάλεκ.d: Peleg, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Φίλιπποι.d: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.

Φίλιππος.d: Philip, (a) one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, (b) tetrarch of the Ituraean and Trachonitic region, half-brother of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, (c) one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem and a missionary.

Φανουήλ.d: Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.

Φαρές.d: Perez, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Φαραώ.d: Pharaoh, the title of ancient Egyptian kings.

Φαρισαῖος.d: a Pharisee, one of the Jewish sect so called.

Φιλήμων.d: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.

Φιλαδέλφεια.d: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia.

Φιλιππήσιος.d: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.

Φοίβη.d: Phoebe, a Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae.

Φοινίκη.d: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.

Φοῖνιξ.d: Phoenix, a bay on the south coast of Crete.

Φρυγία.d: Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor, the north-western part of which was in the Roman province Asia and the south-eastern part in the Roman province Galatia.

Φύγελος.d: Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia who deserted Paul.

Φῆλιξ.d: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52 ?) till A.D. 59.

Χίος.d: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.

Χανάαν.d: Canaan, the whole of Palestine or Palestine west of the river Jordan.

Χαναναῖος.d: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician.

Χλόη.d: Chloe, probably with business connections either in Corinth or in Ephesus or in both.

Χουζᾶς.d: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas.

αἰγιαλός.d: sea-coast, (sandy) beach; shore (of sea or lake), land.

αἰσχροκερδῶς.d: greedily, in a spirit of eagerness for base gain.

αἰσχύνομαι.g: I am ashamed, am put to shame

αἰτία.d: a cause, reason, excuse; a charge, accusation; guilt; circumstances, case.

αἰχμαλωτίζω.d: I take captive (in war); I subdue, ensnare.

αἰών.g: an age, a cycle of time
αἰών.d: an age, a cycle (of time), especially of the present age as contrasted with the future age, and of one of a series of ages stretching to infinity.

αἰώνιος.d: age-long, and therefore: practically eternal, unending; partaking of the character of that which lasts for an age, as contrasted with that which is brief and fleeting.

αἱματεκχυσία.g: a shedding or pouring forth of blood
αἱματεκχυσία.d: a shedding or pouring forth of blood (in sacrifice).

αἱμορροέω.g: I suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood

αἱρετικός.d: disposed to form sects, sectarian, heretical, factious.

αἴρω.d: I raise, lift up, take away, remove.

αἴτιος.g: the cause of, the originator of
αἴτιος.d: the cause, author; the culprit, the accused; the crime.

αἵρεσις.d: a self-chosen opinion, a religious or philosophical sect, discord or contention.

αὐγάζω.d: I flash, gleam, shine forth, appear white, bright; but perhaps: I see, see clearly, discern.

αὐθεντέω.d: I domineer, govern, have mastery over.

αὐλή.d: court-yard, fore-court, sheep-fold; but it may be understood as: palace, house.

αὐλίζομαι.d: I lodge in the open, lodge, pass the night.

αὐξάνω.g: I cause to increase, become greater, grow
αὐξάνω.d: (a) I cause to increase, become greater (b) I increase, grow.

αὐστηρός.d: grim, severe, strict, exacting, harsh, rigid.

αὐτός.g: he, she, it, they, them, same

αὐχμηρός.d: (poetical, lit: dry and parched; then: squalid and rough), dingy, murky, obscure, dark, funereal.

βάθος.d: depth; deep water; met: fullness, immensity; an extreme degree; profundities, deep-laid plans.

βάλλω.g: I cast, throw, rush, put, place, drop
βάλλω.d: (a) I cast, throw, rush, (b) often, in the weaker sense: I place, put, drop.

βάπτισμα.g: the rite or ceremony of baptism

βάρβαρος.g: a foreigner who speaks neither Greek nor Latin
βάρβαρος.d: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin; as adj: foreign.

βάρος.d: a weight, burden, lit. or met.

βήρυλλος.d: a beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green.

βίβλος.g: a written book, roll, or volume
βίβλος.d: a written book, roll, or volume, sometimes with a sacred connotation.

βαθμός.g: a step, a stage, a position
βαθμός.d: a step (of a stairway); hence: a stage in a career, a position.

βαθύς.d: deep (lit. and met.); in the depths of the early morning, while still very early; profound.

βαπτίζω.d: lit: I dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping; I baptize.

βαπτιστής.d: the baptizer, the Baptist, epithet used only of John, the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, forerunner of Jesus.

βαρέω.d: I weight, load, burden, lit. and met.

βαρύς.d: heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met; violent, oppressive.

βασίλειος.g: courtiers, palaces, a body of kings, royal

βασανίζω.d: I examine, as by torture; I torment; I buffet, as of waves.

βασανιστής.g: one who tortures, a tormentor, jailor

βασιλεία.d: kingship, sovereignty, authority, rule, especially of God, both in the world, and in the hearts of men; hence: kingdom, in the concrete sense.

βασιλεύς.d: a king, ruler, but in some passages clearly to be translated: emperor.

βασιλεύω.d: (a) I rule, reign, (b) I reign over.

βασιλικός.g: connected with a king, royal, regal
βασιλικός.d: connected with a king, royal, regal, (a) an officer in the service of the king, (b) the king's country.

βασκαίνω.g: I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower

βαστάζω.d: (a) I carry, bear, (b) I carry (take) away.

βδέλυγμα.g: an abominable thing, an accursed thing

βεβαιόω.d: I confirm, ratify, secure, establish; pass: I guarantee.

βιαστής.d: a forceful, violent man; one who is eager in pursuit.

βλέμμα.d: a look, glance; sight and hearing.

βλέπω.d: (primarily physical), I look, see, perceive, discern.

βλαστάνω.g: I sprout, cause to sprout, make to grow up
βλαστάνω.d: intrans: I sprout; trans: I cause to sprout, make to grow up.

βλασφημέω.d: I speak evil against, blaspheme, use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).

βλητέος.d: a verbal adj: one must put, that ought to be put.

βοήθεια.d: (a) abstr: assistance, (b) concr: (a technical term of nautical language), a help.

βοηθέω.g: I come to the rescue of
βοηθέω.d: I come to the rescue of, come to help, help.

βολή.d: a casting, throw; in acc: as measure of distance.

βολίζω.g: I cast the line for sounding, I sound
βολίζω.d: I cast the line (for sounding), I sound.

βορρᾶς.d: the north wind, hence: the North.

βουλευτής.g: a member of a city council, of the Sanhedrin
βουλευτής.d: a member of a city council, in NT of the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem.

βραβεύω.d: (lit: to act as arbiter in the games), I rule, arbitrate.

βραδύνω.d: I am slow, I delay, tarry.

βρόχος.d: a noose or snare; a cord.

βρύχω.d: I grind or gnash, as with the teeth for rage or pain.

βρύω.g: I cause to gush forth, send forth

βρῶσις.d: (a) abstr: eating, (b) food, a meal, (c) rust.

βυθίζω.d: I cause to sink; mid: I sink, submerge, drown.

βωμός.d: an altar, platform; a slightly-elevated spot.

βῆμα.g: the space covered by a step of the foot, a tribunal
βῆμα.d: an elevated place ascended by steps, a throne, tribunal.

γάμος.d: a marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony; plur: a wedding-feast.

γέ.d: an enclitic, emphasizing particle: at least, indeed, really, but generally too subtle to be represented in English.

γέεννα.d: Gehenna, and originally the name of a valley or cavity near Jerusalem, a place underneath the earth, a place of punishment for evil.

γίνομαι.g: I come into being, am born
γίνομαι.d: I come into being, am born, become, come about, happen.

γαμέω.d: I marry, used of either sex.

γαστήρ.g: the womb, stomach, to be pregnant
γαστήρ.d: the womb, stomach; of a woman: to be with child (lit: to have [a child] in the belly).

γενεά.d: a generation; if repeated twice or with another time word, practically indicates infinity of time.

γενεαλογέομαι.g: I put into a genealogy, reckon my descent

γεννάω.g: I beget, bring forth, give birth to
γεννάω.d: I beget (of the male), (of the female) I bring forth, give birth to.

γερουσία.d: the assembly or body of elders.

γεωργέω.g: I work the soil, cultivate the earth

γεωργός.g: a worker of the soil, husbandman, vine-dresser
γεωργός.d: a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-laborer, vine-dresser.

γινώσκω.g: I come to know, learn, realize
γινώσκω.d: I am taking in knowledge, come to know, learn; aor: I ascertained, realized.

γλεῦκος.d: the unfermented juice of grapes; hence: sweet new wine.

γλωσσόκομον.d: (a vernacular word), bag, purse; some prefer to take as: box, chest.

γλῶσσα.d: the tongue, a language, a nation (usually distinguished by their speech).

γνήσιος.d: (lit: born in wedlock), hence: real, true, genuine; with definite article: the true, genuine element.

γνωρίζω.d: I make known, declare, know, discover.

γογγύζω.d: I whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smoldering discontent).

γονυπετέω.g: I fall on my knees before, supplicate, entreat
γονυπετέω.d: I fall on my knees before (in supplication), supplicate, entreat.

γράμμα.d: a letter of the alphabet; collectively: written (revelation); (a) a written document, a letter, an epistle, (b) writings, literature, learning.

γράφω.d: I write; pass: it is written, it stands written (in the scriptures).

γραμματεύς.g: a scribe, town-clerk, man of learning
γραμματεύς.d: (a) in Jerusalem, a scribe, one learned in the Jewish Law, a religious teacher, (b) at Ephesus, the town-clerk, the secretary of the city, (c) a man of learning generally.

γραφή.g: a writing, passage of scripture, the scriptures
γραφή.d: (a) a writing, (b) a passage of scripture; plur: the scriptures.

γραώδης.g: belonging to old women, such as old women tell

γρηγορέω.g: I am awake, am vigilant, watch
γρηγορέω.d: (a) I am awake (in the night), watch, (b) I am watchful, on the alert, vigilant.

γυμνάζω.d: I train by physical exercise; hence: train, in the widest sense.

γυμνός.d: rarely: stark-naked; generally: wearing only the under-garment; bare, open, manifest; mere.

γυναικάριον.g: a woman, a poor weak woman
γυναικάριον.d: a woman, with all a woman's weakness, a poor weak woman, a silly woman.

γυναικεῖος.d: belonging to woman, of woman, female.

γωνία.d: a corner; met: a secret place.

γόης.d: a conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, imposter.

γῆ.d: the earth, soil, land, region, country, inhabitants of a region.

δάκνω.d: I bite; hence: I backbite, harm seriously.

δέ.g: but, on the other hand, and
δέ.d: a weak adversative particle, generally placed second in its clause; but, on the other hand, and.

δέομαι.d: I want for myself; I want, need; I beg, request, beseech, pray.

δέρμα.d: the skin or hide of an animal.

δέω.d: I bind, tie, fasten; I impel, compel; I declare to be prohibited and unlawful.

δή.d: (a) in a clause expressing demand: so, then, (b) indeed, (c) truly.

δήπου.d: of course, indeed, qualifying and yet strengthening the assertion.

δίδραχμον.d: a double-drachma, two drachmae, a Greek silver coin.

δίδωμι.d: I offer, give; I put, place.

δίκαιος.d: just; especially, just in the eyes of God; righteous; the elect (a Jewish idea).

δίκη.d: (a) (originally: custom, usage) right, justice, (b) process of law, judicial hearing, (c) execution of sentence, punishment, penalty, (d) justice, vengeance.

δίστομος.d: (lit: twain-mouthed; hence: of a sword, as a drinker of blood), two-edged.

δίψυχος.d: (lit: of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering.

δαιμονίζομαι.d: I am possessed, am under the power of an evil-spirit or demon.

δαιμόνιον.d: an evil-spirit, demon; a heathen deity.

δαμάζω.d: I tame, subdue, involving obedience and restraint.

δαπανάω.d: I spend, bear expense, waste, squander.

δείκνυμι.d: I point out, show, exhibit; met: I teach, demonstrate, make known.

δειγματίζω.g: I hold up as an example
δειγματίζω.d: I hold up as an example, make a show of, expose.

δειλιάω.d: I shrink, am fearful, timid, cowardly.

δεισιδαίμων.g: respectful of what is divine, religious
δεισιδαίμων.d: respectful of what is divine; religious, perhaps, rather than superstitious (the usual meaning).

δεισιδαιμονία.d: religion in general; in a bad sense: superstition.

δελεάζω.g: I allure, entice by a bait

δεξιολάβος.g: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man

δεξιός.g: on the right hand, right hand, right

δεσμεύω.d: I bind, put in chains, tie together.

δεσμοφύλαξ.g: a keeper of a prison, a jailer

δεσμός.d: a bond, chain, imprisonment; a string or ligament, an impediment, infirmity.

δευτεραῖος.g: on the second day, on the next day
δευτεραῖος.d: adj. where English requires an adv., on the second day, on the next day.

δεύτερος.g: second, in the second place, for the second time
δεύτερος.d: second; with the article: in the second place, for the second time.

δεῖγμα.d: an example, type; a thing shown.

δεῖνα.g: so and so, such a one
δεῖνα.d: so and so, such a one, where the name of the person is known but not used.

δεῖπνον.g: a dinner, an afternoon or evening meal

δεῦρο.d: (originally: hither, hence) (a) exclamatory: come, (b) temporal: now, the present.

δεῦτε.d: come hither, come, hither, an exclamatory word.

δημηγορέω.g: I make a public speech, address a multitude

δημιουργός.d: an artisan, builder, maker; one who labors for the public.

δηνάριον.d: a denarius, a small Roman silver coin.

διΐστημι.g: I put apart, separate, put some distance between

διά.d: (a) gen: through, throughout, by the instrumentality of, (b) acc: through, on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, because of.

διάβολος.d: (adj. used often as a noun), slanderous; with the article: the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.

διάγνωσις.d: judicial examination, decision; an act of discernment.

διάγω.g: I spend time, pass time, live
διάγω.d: (either trans. or intrans.), I spend time, pass time, live.

διάκονος.d: a waiter, servant; then of any one who performs any service, an administrator.

διάκρισις.d: distinguishing; hence: deciding, passing sentence on; the act of judgment, discernment.

διάλεκτος.d: language, speech, conversation, manner of speaking.

διέξοδος.g: a public spot in a city
διέξοδος.d: a meeting-place of roads, a public spot in a city.

διέρχομαι.g: I pass through, spread a report
διέρχομαι.d: I pass through, spread (as a report).

διαβάλλω.d: I thrust through, slander, complain of, accuse.

διαβαίνω.d: I cross, pass through, step across.

διαγίνομαι.d: I pass (of time); I continue through, intervene.

διαγγέλλω.g: I announce throughout, spread the news of
διαγγέλλω.d: I announce throughout (the world), spread the news of, give notice of, teach.

διαγρηγορέω.g: I awake out of sleep, am thoroughly awake

διαδέχομαι.d: I receive in my turn, receive through another.

διαδίδωμι.g: I offer here and there, distribute, divide
διαδίδωμι.d: I offer here and there, distribute, divide, hand over.

διαζώννυμι.d: I gird, tie around; mid: I gird round myself.

διαθήκη.d: (a) a covenant between two parties, (b) (the ordinary, everyday sense [found a countless number of times in papyri]) a will, testament.

διαιρέω.d: I divide into parts, cut asunder, distribute.

διακονέω.d: I wait at table (particularly of a slave who waits on guests); I serve (generally).

διακονία.d: waiting at table; in a wider sense: service, ministration.

διακούω.g: I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing

διακρίνω.d: I separate, distinguish, discern one thing from another; I doubt, hesitate, waver.

διαλέγομαι.d: I converse, address, preach, lecture; I argue, reason.

διαλαλέω.d: I converse together, talk of; of conversation passing from mouth to mouth.

διαλείπω.g: I cease, give over, give up

διαλλάσσομαι.g: I become reconciled to, reconcile myself with
διαλλάσσομαι.d: I change, exchange; I reconcile, change enmity for friendship.

διαλογισμός.d: a calculation, reasoning, thought, movement of thought, deliberation, plotting.

διαμαρτύρομαι.g: I give solemn evidence, testify solemnly
διαμαρτύρομαι.d: I give solemn evidence, testify (declare) solemnly.

διαμερίζω.g: I divide up into parts, break up, distribute
διαμερίζω.d: I divide up into parts, break up; I distribute.

διανέμω.d: I divide into portions, distribute; pass: I am spread about.

διαπορέω.g: I am in trouble, doubt, difficulty
διαπορέω.d: I am in trouble, doubt, difficulty; I am at a loss.

διαπρίομαι.d: (lit: I saw through), I cut to the quick (with indignation and envy).

διασπορά.d: lit: scattering abroad of seed by the sower, hence: dispersion, used especially of the Jews who had migrated and were scattered over the ancient world.

διαστέλλομαι.d: I give a commission (instructions), order; I admonish, prohibit.

διασῴζω.d: I save (rescue) through (some danger), bring safely to, escaped to.

διατάσσω.d: I give orders to, prescribe, arrange.

διατίθεμαι.d: (a) I appoint, make (of a covenant), (b) I make (a will).

διατρίβω.d: I tarry, continue, stay in a place.

διαυγάζω.d: I shine through, dawn (of the light coming through the shadows).

διαφέρω.g: I carry through, differ, surpass, excel
διαφέρω.d: (a) trans: I carry through, hither and thither, (b) intrans: I am different, differ, and sometimes: I surpass, excel.

διαφθείρω.d: I destroy, waste; hence met: I corrupt.

διαχειρίζομαι.g: I lay my hands upon, slay, kill
διαχειρίζομαι.d: I lay my hands upon, and so: I slay, kill.

διαχωρίζομαι.g: I separate myself from, part from
διαχωρίζομαι.d: I separate myself from, part from, go away.

διδακτικός.g: able to teach, apt to teach

διεγείρω.g: I wake out of sleep, I arouse
διεγείρω.d: I wake out of sleep, arouse in general, stir up.

διετής.d: two years old, lasting two years.

διετία.d: a period of two years, two years; according to ancient practice this means any period between one and two years.

διηγέομαι.d: I relate in full, describe, narrate.

διθάλασσος.d: between two seas, which has sea on both sides.

δικαίωμα.g: a thing pronounced to be just
δικαίωμα.d: a thing pronounced (by God) to be righteous (just, the right); or the restoration of a criminal, a fresh chance given him; a righteous deed, an instance of perfect righteousness.

δικαίωσις.d: acquittal, justifying, justification, a process of absolution.

δικαιοσύνη.d: (usually if not always in a Jewish atmosphere), justice, justness, righteousness, righteousness of which God is the source or author, but practically: a divine righteousness.

δικαιόω.g: I make righteous, defend the cause of, justify
δικαιόω.d: I make righteous, defend the cause of, plead for the righteousness (innocence) of, acquit, justify; hence: I regard as righteous.

διχάζω.g: I set at variance, make to be hostile
διχάζω.d: I cut asunder; met: I set at variance, make to be hostile.

διχοτομέω.g: I cut in two, scourge severely
διχοτομέω.d: I cut in two, perhaps: scourge severely.

διϊκνέομαι.d: I pass through (to), come through (to), pierce.

διϋλίζω.g: I strain, put through a sieve

δογματίζομαι.d: I subject to regulations, decree; mid: I subject myself to regulations, am decree-ridden.

δοκέω.g: I think, seem, appear, it seems

δοκίμιον.g: a test, trial, what is genuine

δοκιμάζω.g: I put to the test, prove, examine
δοκιμάζω.d: I put to the test, prove, examine; I distinguish by testing, approve after testing; I am fit.

δοκιμή.g: a trial, proof; tried, approved character

δοκός.d: a beam or spar of timber.

δολιόω.d: I act deceitfully, deceive, use fraud.

δοξάζω.g: I glorify, honor, bestow glory on

δουλαγωγέω.d: I bring into subjection, enslave, treat as a slave.

δουλεύω.g: I am a slave, am subject to, obey
δουλεύω.d: I am a slave, am subject to, obey, am devoted.

δράκων.d: a dragon or huge serpent; met: Satan.

δράσσομαι.d: I take hold of, grasp, catch.

δραχμή.d: a drachma, a Greek silver coin.

δυνάστης.d: (lit: a man who rules by force), a ruler, potentate; also: courtier, member of the court.

δυναμόω.d: I empower, fill with power, strengthen.

δυνατέω.d: I am powerful, have power, am able, am mighty.

δυνατός.d: (a) of persons: powerful, able, (b) of things: possible.

δυσερμήνευτος.d: difficult to interpret, hard to be understood.

δυσμή.g: a setting of the sun, the West
δυσμή.d: a setting (of the sun), hence: the West.

δυσφημία.d: evil report, defamation, words of ill omen.

δωρεάν.g: as a free gift, without payment, freely

δόξα.d: honor, renown; glory, an especially divine quality, the unspoken manifestation of God, splendor.

δύναμαι.d: (a) I am powerful, have (the) power, (b) I am able, I can.

δύναμις.d: (a) physical power, force, might, ability, efficacy, energy, meaning (b) plur: powerful deeds, deeds showing (physical) power, marvelous works.

δύσκολος.d: difficult, hard; of persons: hard to please.

δώδεκα.d: twelve; the usual way in which the Twelve apostles of Jesus are referred to.

δῆμος.d: properly: the people, especially citizens of a Greek city in popular assembly, but in NT, multitude, rabble.

δῶμα.d: the roof (of a house), the top of the house.

εἰδωλεῖον.d: a temple for (containing) an image (an idol).

εἰδωλολάτρης.d: a server (worshipper) of an image (an idol).

εἰδωλόθυτον.d: (of meat), sacrificed to an image (or an idol).

εἰκῇ.d: without a cause, purpose; purposelessly, in vain, for nothing.

εἰρήνη.d: peace, peace of mind; invocation of peace a common Jewish farewell, in the Hebraistic sense of the health (welfare) of an individual.

εἰρηνεύω.g: I am peaceful, keep the peace, am at peace

εἰς.d: into, in, unto, to, upon, towards, for, among.

εἰσάγω.d: I lead in, bring in, introduce.

εἰσέρχομαι.g: I go in, come in, enter

εἰσκαλέομαι.d: I call in (to my house), invite.

εἰσπορεύομαι.d: I journey in(to), I go in(to), enter, intervene.

εἰσφέρω.d: I lead into, bring in, announce.

εἴσειμι.d: I go in, enter (originally: I shall go in).

εἴωθα.g: I am accustomed, custom, what was customary

εἶδος.d: visible form, shape, appearance, outward show, kind, species, class.

εἶτα.d: then, thereafter, next (marking a fresh stage); therefore, then, furthermore.

εὐαγγέλιον.d: the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel; the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, etc.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).

εὐαγγελίζω.g: I bring good news, preach good tidings
εὐαγγελίζω.d: I bring good news, preach good tidings, with or without an object, expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person).

εὐαγγελιστής.g: an evangelist, bearer of good tidings
εὐαγγελιστής.d: an evangelist, a missionary, bearer of good tidings.

εὐαρεστέω.d: I give pleasure to, please (perhaps with the added idea of: rendering good service to).

εὐγενής.d: (a) of noble birth, of high birth, (b) noble in nature.

εὐδοκέω.d: I am well-pleased, think it good, am resolved.

εὐδοκία.d: (a) good-will (good-pleasure), favor, feeling of complacency of God to man, (b) good-pleasure, satisfaction, happiness, delight of men.

εὐεργεσία.d: good action, well-doing, benefiting, kind service.

εὐεργετέω.d: I do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit.

εὐθυμέω.d: I keep up spirit, am cheerful, am of good courage.

εὐθύνω.d: (a) I make straight (of the direction, not the surface, of a road), (b) I guide, steer.

εὐθύς.d: adj: (a) straight of direction, as opposed to crooked, (b) upright; adv: immediately.

εὐκαιρέω.g: I have a good opportunity, have leisure
εὐκαιρέω.d: I have a good (favorable) opportunity, have leisure; I devote my leisure to.

εὐλαβέομαι.d: I fear, am anxious, am cautious; I reverence.

εὐλαβής.d: (lit: handling well, hence) cautious, circumspect; hence: God-fearing, pious.

εὐλογέω.d: (lit: I speak well of) I bless; pass: I am blessed.

εὐλογητός.d: (used only of God), blessed (as entitled to receive blessing from man), worthy of praise.

εὐμετάδοτος.d: willingly sharing, ready to impart, generous.

εὐνουχίζω.d: I make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate.

εὐνοῦχος.g: a eunuch, keeper of the bed-chamber
εὐνοῦχος.d: (a) a chamberlain, keeper of the bed-chamber of an eastern potentate, eunuch, (b) a eunuch, castrated person, or one who voluntarily abstains from marriage.

εὐοδόομαι.g: I cause to prosper, have a happy journey
εὐοδόομαι.d: I cause to prosper, pass: I have a happy (successful) journey, hence: I prosper.

εὐπορέομαι.d: I have means, am prosperous, enjoy plenty.

εὐπροσωπέω.g: I make a fair outward appearance
εὐπροσωπέω.d: I look well, make a fair show (a good outward appearance, and so win good opinion).

εὐσεβέω.d: I am dutiful, pious, show piety towards, worship.

εὐσχήμων.d: (a) comely, seemly, decorous, (b) of honorable position (in society), wealthy, influential.

εὐφορέω.g: I bear well, bring a good harvest
εὐφορέω.d: I bear well, bring a good harvest, yield abundantly.

εὐφραίνω.g: I cheer, am glad, make merry
εὐφραίνω.d: I cheer, make glad; generally mid. or pass: I am glad, make merry, revel, feast.

εὐχή.d: a prayer comprising a vow; a prayer, vow.

εὐχαριστέω.d: I thank, give thanks; pass. 3 sing: is received with thanks.

εὐχαριστία.d: thankfulness, gratitude; giving of thanks, thanksgiving.

εὐώνυμος.d: (lit: well-named, to avoid the evil omen attaching to the left), on the left-hand side, left.

εὑρίσκω.d: I find, learn, discover, especially after searching.

εὔκαιρος.d: opportune, timely, suitable; perhaps sometimes: holiday, festival.

εὔσημος.d: with clear meaning, intelligible, clear to the understanding.

εὔφημος.g: well reported of, spoken in a kindly spirit
εὔφημος.d: well reported of, spoken in a kindly spirit, laudable, reputable.

εὖ.d: well, well done, good, rightly; also used as an exclamation.

ζέω.d: (lit: I boil, am boiling), I burn (in spirit), am fervent.

ζήτημα.d: a question, subject of inquiry, dispute.

ζήτησις.d: a question, debate, controversy; a seeking, search.

ζεῦγος.d: a yoke, team; hence: a pair.

ζηλωτής.d: one who is eagerly devoted to a person or a thing, a zealot.

ζηλόω.d: (a) intrans: I am jealous, (b) trans: I am jealous of, with acc. of a person; I am eager for, am eager to possess, with acc. of a thing.

ζημιόω.d: I inflict loss (damage) upon, fine, punish, sometimes with the acc. of the penalty, even when the verb is passive.

ζητέω.d: I seek, search for, desire, require, demand.

ζιζάνιον.d: spurious wheat, darnel; a plant that grows in Palestine which resembles wheat in many ways but is worthless.

ζυγός.g: a yoke, heavy burden, pair of scales
ζυγός.d: a yoke; hence met: (a Jewish idea) of a heavy burden, comparable to the heavy yokes resting on the bullocks' necks; a balance, pair of scales.

ζωή.d: life, both of physical (present) and of spiritual (particularly future) existence.

ζωγρέω.d: I capture alive, capture for life, enthrall.

ζύμη.d: leaven, ferment, both lit. and met.

ζώνη.d: a girdle, belt, waistband; because the purse was kept there, also: a purse.

ζώννυμι.d: I gird, put on the girdle, especially as preparatory to active work.

ζῳογονέω.d: I preserve alive (lit: bring to birth), save.

ζῳοποιέω.d: I make that which was dead to live, cause to live, quicken.

θάλασσα.d: (a) the sea, in contrast to the land, (b) a particular sea or lake, e.g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.

θάλπω.d: (properly: I warm, then) I cherish, nourish, foster, comfort.

θάμβος.d: astonishment, amazement (allied to terror or awe).

θέατρον.d: (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky, (b) a spectacle, show.

θέλημα.d: an act of will, will; plur: wishes, desires.

θέλω.d: I will, wish, desire, am willing, intend, design.

θήκη.d: a repository, receptacle; a case, sheath, scabbard.

θήρα.d: hunting, entrapping; prey, game; a net, means of capture.

θαμβέομαι.d: I amaze; pass: I am amazed (almost terrified).

θανατόω.d: I put to death, subdue; pass: I am in danger of death, am dead to, am rid of, am parted from.

θαρρέω.g: I am courageous, of good cheer
θαρρέω.d: I am courageous, confident, of good cheer.

θαρσέω.d: I am of good courage, good cheer, am bold.

θαυμάζω.d: (a) intrans: I wonder, marvel, (b) trans: I wonder at, admire.

θαυμαστός.d: to be wondered at, wonderful, marvelous.

θαῦμα.d: (a) concr: a marvel, wonder, (b) abstr: wonder, amazement.

θεάομαι.d: I see, behold, contemplate, look upon, view; I see, visit.

θεατρίζω.g: I make a public show of
θεατρίζω.d: I make a public show of, expose to public shame.

θεμέλιος.d: (properly, an adj: belonging to the foundation), a foundation stone.

θεμελιόω.d: I found, lay the foundation (lit. and met.).

θεοσέβεια.d: reverence for God, fear of God, godliness, piety.

θεραπεία.d: care, attention, especially medical attention (treatment); hence almost: healing; meton: those who render service.

θεραπεύω.g: I care for, attend, serve, heal
θεραπεύω.d: I care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence: I heal.

θερισμός.d: reaping, harvest; met: the harvest, crop.

θερμαίνομαι.d: I warm; mid: I warm myself.

θεωρέω.d: I look at, gaze, behold; I see, experience, discern; I partake of.

θεόπνευστος.d: God-breathed, inspired by God, due to the inspiration of God.

θηρίον.d: properly: a wild beast, hence: any animal; met: a brute.

θηρεύω.d: I hunt, seek to catch or entrap; met: I lay hold of.

θηριομαχέω.d: I fight with wild beasts (i.e. wild beasts in human form); met: I am exposed to fierce hostility.

θησαυρίζω.g: I store up, treasure up, save
θησαυρίζω.d: I store up, treasure up, save, lay up.

θησαυρός.d: a store-house for precious things; hence: a treasure, a store.

θλίβω.g: I make narrow, persecute, press hard
θλίβω.d: (a) I make narrow (strictly: by pressure); I press upon, (b) I persecute, press hard.

θνῄσκω.d: I die, am dying, am dead.

θορυβέω.g: I disturb greatly, terrify, strike with panic
θορυβέω.d: I disturb greatly, terrify, strike with panic; mid: I show agitation of mind.

θρέμμα.d: (lit: a nursling, hence probably) plur: cattle.

θρίξ.d: hair (of the head or of animals).

θραύω.d: I crush, break, shatter; met: I break down.

θρηνέω.d: intrans: I lament, wail; trans: I bewail.

θρησκεία.d: (underlying sense: reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.

θρησκός.d: (refers probably to a careful observance of religious restrictions), religious (probably in a limited sense), devout.

θριαμβεύω.g: I lead around, make a spectacle of
θριαμβεύω.d: (properly: I lead one as my prisoner in a triumphal procession, hence) I lead around, make a show (spectacle) of, cause to triumph.

θροέομαι.d: I disturb, agitate; pass: I am troubled, alarmed.

θρόνος.d: a (king's) throne, seat; meton: power, dominion; a potentate.

θυγάτηρ.d: a daughter; hence (Hebraistic?), of any female descendent, however far removed; even of one unrelated: my young lady.

θυμιατήριον.d: (ordinarily: censer, but) either the altar of incense, or the shovel, on which the high-priest poured the coals, when he entered the Holy of Holies on the Day of Atonement.

θυμομαχέω.d: (lit: I fight desperately, hence) I am furiously angry with.

θυμόομαι.g: I provoke to anger, am full of angry passion
θυμόομαι.d: I provoke to anger; pass: I am wroth or very angry.

θυσία.d: abstr. and concr: sacrifice; a sacrifice, offering.

θόρυβος.d: (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, outcry, (b) riot, disturbance.

θύω.d: I sacrifice, generally an animal; hence: I kill.

κάθημαι.d: I sit, am seated, enthroned; I dwell, reside.

κάλαμος.d: a reed; a reed-pen, reed-staff, measuring rod.

κάλυμμα.d: a covering, especially a covering of head and face, a veil.

κάμνω.d: I work, am weary, am sick.

κάρφος.g: a dry stalk, chip of wood
κάρφος.d: a dry stalk, chip of wood, twig, splinter, chaff.

κάτω.d: (a) down, below, also: downwards, (b) lower, under, less, of a length of time.

κέλευσμα.g: a word of command, a call
κέλευσμα.d: a word of command, a call, an arousing outcry.

κέντρον.d: a sting, goad; met: of death.

κέρας.d: (a) a horn, (b) a horn-like projection at the corner of an altar, (c) a horn as a symbol of power.

κέρμα.d: a small coin; plur: small change.

καίω.d: I ignite, light, burn, lit. and met; I consume with fire.

καθάπτω.g: I lay hold of, fasten on to
καθάπτω.d: I lay hold of, fasten on to, seize, attack.

καθέζομαι.g: I am sitting, sit, am seated
καθέζομαι.d: I am sitting, sit down, am seated.

καθήκω.d: I come down, come to; I am unfit, proper.

καθίζω.d: (a) trans: I make to sit; I set, appoint, (b) intrans: I sit down, am seated, stay.

καθίστημι.d: I set down, bring down to a place; I set in order, appoint, make, constitute.

καθαιρέω.d: (a) I take down, pull down, depose, destroy.

καθαρίζω.d: I cleanse, make clean, literally, ceremonially, or spiritually, according to context.

καθαρισμός.d: cleansing, purifying, purification, literal, ceremonial, or moral; met: expiation.

καθαρός.d: clean, pure, unstained, either literally or ceremonially or spiritually; guiltless, innocent, upright.

καθεξῆς.d: in order, in succession, in the time immediately after, just after.

καθό.d: according to which thing, as, according as.

καθόλου.d: one the whole, in general, altogether.

καθότι.d: (a) in proportion as, according as, (b) because.

καθώς.d: according to the manner in which, in the degree that, just as, as.

καιρός.d: fitting season, season, opportunity, occasion, time.

κακία.d: (a) evil (i.e. trouble, labor, misfortune), (b) wickedness, (c) vicious disposition, malice, spite.

κακολογέω.d: I speak evil of, curse, revile, abuse.

κακοποιέω.d: I do harm, do wrong, do evil, commit sin.

κακός.d: bad, evil, in the widest sense.

κακόω.d: I treat badly, afflict, embitter, make angry.

καλέω.d: (a) I call, summon, invite, (b) I call, name.

καλοδιδάσκαλος.g: a teacher of that which is noble
καλοδιδάσκαλος.d: a teacher of that which is noble (honorable) and good.

καλοποιέω.d: I do well, act honorably, do what is right.

καλός.d: beautiful, as an outward sign of the inward good, noble, honorable character; good, worthy, honorable, noble, and seen to be so.

κανών.d: (lit: a level, ruler), a rule, regulation, rule of conduct or doctrine, (b) a measured (defined) area, province.

καπηλεύω.d: I hawk, trade in, deal in for purposes of gain.

καρδία.d: lit: the heart; mind, character, inner self, will, intention, center.

καρδιογνώστης.g: a knower of the inner life
καρδιογνώστης.d: a knower of the inner life (character, hearts).

καρπός.d: (a) fruit, generally vegetable, sometimes animal, (b) met: fruit, deed, action, result, (c) profit, gain.

καρτερέω.d: I persevere, endure, am steadfast, patient.

κατά.g: down from, against, according to, throughout, during
κατά.d: gen: against, down from, throughout, by; acc: over against, among, daily, day-by-day, each day, according to, by way of.

κατάγνυμι.d: I break down (in pieces), crush, break into.

κατάγω.d: I lead down, bring down, either from a high place on land or to a lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to land.

κατάκειμαι.d: I recline (at table); more often: I keep my bed, am lying ill (in bed).

κατάκριμα.d: punishment following condemnation, penal servitude, penalty.

κατάλαλος.d: slanderous, back-biting; subst: a railer, defamer.

κατάλοιπος.d: left behind; the rest, the remainder.

κατάπαυσις.d: (in the Old Testament of the rest attained by the settlement in Canaan), resting, rest, dwelling, habitation.

κατάρα.d: cursing; a curse; meton: a doomed one.

κατέρχομαι.d: I come down from sky to earth, or from high land to lower land (or to the coast), or from the high seas to the shore.

κατέχω.d: (a) I hold fast, bind, arrest, (b) I take possession of, lay hold of, (c) I hold back, detain, restrain, (d) I hold a ship, keep its head.

κατήφεια.d: a downcast countenance as a sign of sorrow, gloominess, gloom, dejection.

καταβάλλω.d: (a) mid: I lay, of a foundation, (b) met: I cast down, prostrate.

καταβαίνω.d: I go down, come down, either from the sky or from higher land, descend.

καταβιβάζω.g: I bring down, cause to go down
καταβιβάζω.d: I bring down, cast down, cause to go down.

καταβολή.d: (a) foundation, (b) depositing, sowing, deposit, technically used of the act of conception.

καταβραβεύω.d: of the umpire in a contest: I decide against, take part against, condemn (perhaps with the idea of assumption, officialism).

καταγγέλλω.d: I declare openly, proclaim, preach, laud, celebrate.

καταγωνίζομαι.d: I subdue (in warfare); I struggle against, conquer, overcome.

καταισχύνω.g: I shame, disgrace, put to utter confusion
καταισχύνω.d: I shame, disgrace, bring to shame, put to utter confusion, frustrate.

κατακλάω.d: I break in pieces, break up.

κατακλίνω.d: I cause to recline at table; mid. and pass: I recline at table.

κατακληρονομέω.d: I give as an inheritance, distribute by lot.

κατακρίνω.d: I condemn, judge worthy of punishment.

κατακρημνίζω.d: I cast down headlong, throw over a precipice.

κατακυριεύω.d: I exercise authority over, overpower, master.

κατακόπτω.d: I cut up, cut in pieces, mangle, wound.

καταλέγω.g: I enter in a list, register
καταλέγω.d: I enter in a list, register, enroll.

καταλαλέω.d: I speak evil of, rail at, slander.

καταλαμβάνω.g: I seize tight hold of, overtake, comprehend
καταλαμβάνω.d: (a) I seize tight hold of, arrest, catch, capture, appropriate, (b) I overtake, (c) mid. aor: I perceived, comprehended.

καταλείπω.d: I leave behind, desert, abandon, forsake; I leave remaining, reserve.

καταλιθάζω.g: I stone down, stone to death
καταλιθάζω.d: I stone down, stone to death, overwhelm with stones.

καταλύω.g: I break up, overthrow, unharness, find a lodging
καταλύω.d: (lit: I loosen thoroughly), (a) trans: I break up, overthrow, destroy, both lit. and met., (b) I unyoke, unharness a carriage horse or pack animal; hence: I put up, lodge, find a lodging.

καταμένω.d: I wait, stay (with), remain, abide, dwell.

καταμανθάνω.d: I understand, take in a fact about, consider carefully.

καταναλίσκω.d: I use up, spend, consume (as with fire).

καταναρκάω.d: (properly a medical term: I stupefy, hence) I burden, encumber.

κατανεύω.d: I nod, make a sign, beckon.

κατανοέω.d: I take note of, perceive, consider carefully, discern, detect, make account of.

καταντάω.g: I come down, arrive at, reach
καταντάω.d: (a) I come down, either from high land to lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to the coast; hence met: I arrive at, reach (my destination), (b) of property: I come down (descend) by inheritance to an heir.

κατανύσσομαι.d: met: I am pierced, stung, smitten.

καταπέτασμα.d: (lit: that which is spread out downwards, that which hangs down), a curtain, veil, of that which separated the Holy of Holies from the outer parts of the temple at Jerusalem, also of an outer curtain at the entrance to the Holy Place in the same temple.

καταπίνω.d: I drink down, swallow, devour, destroy, consume.

καταπατέω.d: I trample down, trample under foot (lit. and met.), spurn.

καταπαύω.d: (a) trans: I cause to rest, bring to rest; I cause to refrain, (b) intrans: I rest.

καταπλέω.d: I sail down (from the high seas to the shore).

καταπονέω.d: I exhaust by labor or suffering, wear out, overpower, oppress.

καταποντίζομαι.g: I sink in the sea, am drowned
καταποντίζομαι.d: I sink in the sea, pass: I drown, am submerged.

καταργέω.g: I bring to naught, sever, abolish
καταργέω.d: (a) I make idle (inactive), make of no effect, annul, abolish, bring to naught, (b) I discharge, sever, separate from.

καταρτίζω.d: (a) I fit (join) together; met: I compact together, (b) act. and mid: I prepare, perfect, for his (its) full destination or use, bring into its proper condition (whether for the first time, or after a lapse).

καταρτισμός.d: a bringing to a condition of fitness, perfecting.

κατασείω.d: I shake (the hand) up and down, wave; intrans: I beckon for silence.

κατασκάπτω.d: I dig down under, demolish, undermine.

κατασκευάζω.d: I build, construct, prepare, make ready.

κατασκηνόω.d: I encamp, take up my quarters, tabernacle, pitch my tent, dwell.

κατασκοπέω.d: I view closely, inspect, spy out.

καταστέλλω.d: I let down, lower; I keep down, restrain, pacify.

καταστρώννυμι.d: I strew or spread over; I lay low, overthrow.

κατασφραγίζω.d: I seal up, secure with a seal.

κατατίθημι.d: (a) I lay down, deposit, (b) mid: I lay down or deposit a favor, with the view of receiving one in return, seek favor.

καταφέρω.d: I bear down, overpower; I give a vote or verdict, bring charges.

καταφεύγω.d: I flee for refuge (implying that the refuge is reached); aor. indicates moment of arrival.

καταφρονέω.d: I despise, scorn, and show it by active insult, disregard.

καταχράομαι.d: I use to the full, use up.

κατείδωλος.d: full of images of idols, grossly idolatrous.

κατενώπιον.d: before the face of, over against.

κατεργάζομαι.d: I effect by labor, achieve, work out, bring about.

κατεσθίω.g: I eat till it is finished
κατεσθίω.d: I eat up, eat till it is finished, devour, squander, annoy, injure.

κατευθύνω.d: (a) I make straight, (b) met: I put in the right way, direct.

κατεφίστημι.d: I rush, assault, rise up against.

κατισχύω.g: I prevail against, overpower, am able
κατισχύω.d: I prevail against, overpower, get the upper hand.

κατιόομαι.d: I rust; pass: I am rusted, tarnished.

κατοικέω.g: I dwell in, settle in, inhabit
κατοικέω.d: I dwell in, settle in, am established in (permanently), inhabit.

καύχημα.d: a boasting; a ground of boasting (glorying, exultation).

καύχησις.d: the act of boasting, glorying, exultation.

κείρω.g: I shear, cut the hair of
κείρω.d: I shear, cut the hair of; mid: I cut my own hair, have my hair cut.

κειρία.d: a kind of girdle made of cords; a bandage, grave clothes.

κεντυρίων.d: a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.

κενός.d: (a) empty, (b) met: empty (in moral content), vain, ineffective, foolish, worthless, (c) false, unreal, pretentious, hollow.

κενόω.g: I empty, deprive of content, make unreal
κενόω.d: (a) I empty, (b) I deprive of content, make unreal.

κενῶς.d: falsely, in vain, to no purpose.

κεράννυμι.g: I mix, pour out for drinking
κεράννυμι.d: I mix, mingle, pour out for drinking.

κεραία.d: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other little letters, or a separation stroke between letters.

κεραμικός.g: of clay, made by a potter
κεραμικός.d: of clay, made by a potter, earthen.

κερδαίνω.d: I gain, acquire, win (over), avoid loss.

κερματιστής.d: properly: a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer.

κεφάλαιον.g: the chief matter, a sum of money
κεφάλαιον.d: (a) the chief matter, the main point, (b) a sum of money.

κεφαλή.d: (a) the head, (b) met: a corner stone, uniting two walls; head, ruler, lord.

κεφαλίς.d: (lit: little head, then: the knob at the end of the wooden core of a roll of papyrus, then) a roll, volume, division (of a book).

κεῖμαι.d: I lie, recline, am placed, am laid, set, specially appointed, destined.

κιβωτός.d: (properly: a wooden box, hence) the Ark, in which Noah sailed; the Ark of the Covenant.

κιθαρίζω.d: intrans. and trans: I play on the harp, I harp, with acc. of the tune.

κιθαρῳδός.d: a harpist, one who sings with harp as accompaniment.

κινέω.d: I set in motion, move, remove, excite, stir up.

κινδυνεύω.d: I am in danger or peril.

κλάδος.d: a young tender shoot, then: a branch; met: of descendants.

κλέος.d: glory, fame, praise; rumor, report, credit.

κλίμα.d: a small geographical division, district, or territory.

κλίνη.d: a couch, bed, portable bed or mat, a couch for reclining at meals, possibly also a bier.

κλίνω.g: I rest, recline, make to yield
κλίνω.d: trans: I rest, recline; I bend, incline; I cause to give ground, make to yield; intrans: I decline, approach my end.

κλαίω.d: I weep, weep for, mourn, lament.

κληρονομέω.d: I inherit, obtain (possess) by inheritance, acquire.

κληρονομία.d: an inheritance, an heritage, regularly the gift of God to His chosen people, in the Old Testament: the Promised Land, in NT a possession viewed in one sense as present, in another as future; a share, participation.

κληρόω.d: I cast lots, choose by lot, assign by lot, assign a portion, receive a share.

κλητός.d: called, invited, summoned by God to an office or to salvation.

κλινίδιον.d: a couch or litter of a sick person.

κλισία.g: a dining couch, group of diners
κλισία.d: properly: a dining couch; hence: a group of diners.

κλυδωνίζομαι.d: I am tossed by waves, met: I am tossed to and fro.

κλύδων.d: rough water, a wave, billow, surge.

κλῆρος.d: (a) a lot, (b) a portion assigned; hence: a portion of the people of God assigned to one's care, a congregation.

κλῆσις.d: a calling, invitation; in the NT, always of a divine call.

κνήθομαι.d: I rub, tickle, scratch; pass: I itch.

κοίτη.d: (a) a bed, (b) a marriage bed; plur: repeated (immoral) sexual intercourse.

κοδράντης.d: a "quadrans," the smallest Roman copper coin, a quarter of an "as," the sixteenth part of a "sesterius".

κοιλία.d: belly, abdomen, heart, a general term covering any organ in the abdomen, e.g. stomach, womb; met: the inner man.

κοιμάομαι.d: I fall asleep, am asleep, sometimes of the sleep of death.

κοινωνέω.g: I share, communicate, have fellowship with
κοινωνέω.d: (a) I share, communicate, contribute, impart, (b) I share in, have a share of, have fellowship with.

κοινωνία.d: (lit: partnership) (a) contributory help, participation, (b) sharing in, communion, (c) spiritual fellowship, a fellowship in the spirit.

κοινωνικός.d: willing to share, sociable, ready to communicate, beneficent.

κοινός.d: (a) common, shared, (b) Hebraistic use: profane; dirty, unclean, unwashed.

κοινόω.g: I make unclean, regard as unclean
κοινόω.d: I make unclean, pollute, desecrate, mid: I regard (treat) as unclean.

κολάζω.d: I chastise, curtail, punish; mid: I cause to be punished.

κολακεία.d: flattery, with a view to advantage or gain.

κολαφίζω.g: I strike with the fist, maltreat
κολαφίζω.d: I strike with the fist, buffet; hence: I mistreat violently.

κολλάομαι.g: I glue, cleave, keep company with
κολλάομαι.d: (lit: I glue); hence: mid. and pass: I join myself closely, cleave, adhere (to), I keep company (with), of friendly intercourse.

κολλυβιστής.d: a money-changer, who changed heathen into Jewish money, for payment into the Temple treasury.

κολοβόω.d: (lit: I maim, mutilate), I cut short, shorten, abbreviate.

κολυμβήθρα.d: (lit: a diving or swimming place), a pool.

κολωνία.d: a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.

κομάω.d: I wear the hair long, allow the hair to grow out.

κομίζω.d: (a) act: I convey, bring, carry, (b) mid: I receive back, receive what has belonged to myself but has been lost, or else promised but kept back, or: I get what has come to be my own by earning, recover.

κοπάζω.d: I abate, cease raging, am stilled.

κοπετός.d: beating of the breast or head in lamentation, lamentation.

κοπιάω.d: (a) I grow weary, (b) I toil, work with effort (of bodily and mental labor alike).

κοράσιον.d: a little girl, a young girl; a girl, maiden.

κορέννυμι.d: I fill, sate, glut, feed full, satisfy.

κοσμέω.d: I put into order; I decorate, deck, adorn.

κοσμικός.d: earthly, worldly (belonging to the present earthly world as opposed to the heavenly and future).

κοσμοκράτωρ.d: ruler of this world, that is, of the world as asserting its independence of God; used of the angelic or demonic powers controlling the sublunary world.

κράβαττος.d: a bed, mattress, mat of a poor man.

κράτιστος.d: most excellent, an official epithet, used in addressing a Roman of high rank, and in the second century one of equestrian (as distinguished from senatorial) rank.

κράτος.d: dominion, strength, power; a mighty deed.

κρέας.d: flesh; plur: pieces of flesh, kinds of flesh.

κρίμα.d: (a) a judgment, a verdict; sometimes implying an adverse verdict, a condemnation, (b) a case at law, a lawsuit.

κρίνον.d: a lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the whole lily, the sword lily.

κρίνω.d: (a) I judge, whether in a law-court or privately: sometimes with cognate nouns emphasizing the notion of the verb, (b) I decide, I think (it) good.

κρίσις.d: judging, judgment, decision, sentence; generally: divine judgment; accusation.

κρατέω.d: I am strong, mighty, hence: I rule, am master, prevail; I obtain, take hold of; I hold, hold fast.

κραταιόομαι.d: I strengthen, confirm; pass: I grow strong, become strong.

κραυγή.d: (a) a shout, cry, clamor, (b) outcry, clamoring against another.

κρεμάννυμι.d: I hang, hang up, suspend; mid: I am hanging, hang.

κριτήριον.d: criterion; a law-court; a law-case before an arbiter; a cause, controversy.

κριτικός.d: critical, able to judge or discern.

κρούω.d: I knock, beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance.

κρυπτός.d: hidden, secret; as subst: the hidden (secret) things (parts), the inward nature (character).

κρυσταλλίζω.d: I am clear as crystal, brilliant like crystal.

κρύπτη.d: a cellar, vault, hidden place, crypt.

κτάομαι.d: (a) I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy, (b) I possess, win mastery over.

κτίζω.d: I create, form, shape, make, always of God.

κτίσις.d: (often of the founding of a city), (a) abstr: creation, (b) concr: creation, creature, institution; always of Divine work, (c) an institution, ordinance.

κτίστης.d: (often of the founder of a city), creator, God.

κτῆμα.d: a piece of landed property, a field; plur: possessions, property, possibly landed property, property in land.

κτῆνος.d: a beast of burden (generally, a horse or mule) either for riding or for carrying loads on its back, or for yoking to a cart or carriage.

κυβεία.d: (lit: playing with dice, gaming, hence) trickery, sleight.

κυβερνήτης.d: a steersman, pilot; met: a guide, governor.

κυκλόθεν.d: in a circle round, round about.

κυλλός.d: crippled, lame, especially in the hands.

κυνάριον.d: a little dog, a house dog.

κυριακός.d: of the Lord, special to the Lord.

κυριότης.d: (a) abstr: lordship, (b) concr: divine or angelic lordship, domination, dignity, usually with reference to a celestial hierarchy.

κυρόω.d: I ratify, confirm, make valid, reaffirm, assure.

κωλύω.d: I prevent, debar, hinder; with infin: from doing so and so.

κωμόπολις.d: a large village, a city which in constitution has only the status of a village; a country town.

κόκκινος.d: crimson, scarlet, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak.

κόλασις.d: chastisement, punishment, torment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation.

κόλπος.g: bosom, bosom of a garment, a bay, gulf
κόλπος.d: (a) sing. and plur: bosom; (sinus) the overhanging fold of the garment used as a pocket, (b) a bay, gulf.

κόπος.d: (a) trouble, (b) toil, labor, laborious toil, involving weariness and fatigue.

κόπτω.d: (a) I cut, cut off, strike, smite, (b) mid: I beat my breast or head in lamentation, lament, mourn, sometimes with acc. of person whose loss is mourned.

κόσμος.d: the world, universe; worldly affairs; the inhabitants of the world; adornment.

κύμινον.d: cumin, a plant used as a spice.

κύπτω.d: I bend, stoop down, bow the head.

κύων.d: a dog, universally despised in the East.

κώνωψ.d: a gnat, mosquito, referred to proverbially as something small.

κἀγώ.d: I also, I too, but I.

κἀκεῖ.d: and there, and yonder, there also.

κἀκεῖθεν.d: and thence, and from there; and then afterwards.

κἀκεῖνος.g: and he, she, it, and that

κἄν.d: and if, even if, even, at least.

κῆπος.d: a garden, any place planted with trees and herbs.

κῆτος.d: a sea monster, huge sea fish, whale.

κῶλον.d: a limb, member of a body; fig: a corpse, carcass.

λέγω.d: (denoting speech in progress), (a) I say, speak; I mean, mention, tell, (b) I call, name, especially in the pass., (c) I tell, command.

λίθος.d: a stone; met: of Jesus as the chief stone in a building.

λίτρα.d: a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces.

λίψ.d: the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.

λαγχάνω.g: I obtain by lot, cast lots
λαγχάνω.d: (a) I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is, (b) I draw lots.

λαλέω.d: (I talk, chatter in classical Greek, but in NT a more dignified word) I speak, say.

λαλιά.d: (in classical Greek: babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech, dialect.

λαμβάνω.d: (a) I receive, get, (b) I take, lay hold of.

λανθάνω.d: I am hidden (concealed), lie hid, escape notice, sometimes with acc. of person from whom concealment takes place; I do so and so unconsciously, unknown to myself, I shut my eyes to so and so.

λατρεία.d: service rendered to God, perhaps simply: worship.

λατρεύω.d: I serve, especially God, perhaps simply: I worship.

λαός.d: (a) a people, characteristically of God's chosen people, first the Jews, then the Christians, (b) sometimes, but rarely, the people, the crowd.

λαῖλαψ.d: a sudden storm, squall, whirlwind, hurricane.

λείπω.g: I am wanting, am left behind
λείπω.d: (earlier: I leave behind, abandon), (a) I am wanting, (b) mid: e.g. with gen: I come behind (in a race), am left behind in, fall short of (some standard), am wanting in.

λειτουργέω.d: I act in the public service, render service, minister, in the widest sense, of some special public religious service, but also of the service of priests and Levites.

λειτουργία.d: a charitable gift, public service in the widest sense; service as of priest or Levite ritual.

λειτουργός.d: a minister, servant, of an official character; of priests and Levites.

λεπίς.d: a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.

λεπτόν.d: a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money.

λιθοβολέω.d: I stone, cast stones (at), kill by stoning.

λικμάω.d: I crush to powder, scatter like chaff.

λογίζομαι.d: I reckon, count, charge with; reason, decide, conclude; think, suppose.

λογικός.d: (a) reasonable, rational, (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with the literal.

λογομαχία.d: contention about words, an unprofitable controversy.

λοιδορέω.d: I revile a person to his face, abuse insultingly.

λοιπός.d: left, left behind, the remainder, the rest, the others.

λουτρόν.d: a bath (of water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.

λούω.d: (lit. or merely ceremonially), I wash, bathe (the body); mid: of washing, bathing one's self; met: I cleanse from sin.

λυτρόομαι.d: I release on receipt of ransom; mid: I redeem, release by paying ransom, liberate.

λόγιον.d: plur: oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire Old Testament).

λόγος.g: a word, speech, divine utterance, analogy

λύκος.d: a wolf, of perhaps a jackal; often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.

λύτρον.g: a ransom, an offering of expiation
λύτρον.d: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.

λύτρωσις.d: (in the Old Testament: ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, etc.), liberation, deliverance, release.

λύω.d: (a) I loose, untie, release, (b) met: I break, destroy, set at naught, contravene; I break up a meeting, annul.

μάγος.d: a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard.

μάννα.d: (Hebrew), manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites in the desert: of spiritual food.

μάρτυς.d: a witness; an eye- or ear-witness.

μάστιξ.d: (a) a scourge, lash, of leathern thongs with pieces of metal sewn up in them, (b) met: severe pains (sufferings), disease.

μάταιος.d: vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive; practically: godless.

μάτην.d: in vain, in an unreal way, to no purpose.

μάχη.d: (earlier: a battle, conflict, hence) in the sphere of words, etc: strife, contention, quarrel.

μάχομαι.g: I engage in battle, fight, strive
μάχομαι.d: I engage in battle, fight; hence: I strive, contend, dispute.

μέγας.d: large, great, in the widest sense.

μέλει.g: it is a care, it concerns
μέλει.d: it is a care, it is an object of anxiety, it concerns.

μέλλω.d: I intend, am about to; I delay, linger.

μέν.d: an untranslatable particle, generally answered by "de", each of the two introducing a clause intended to be contrasted with the other.

μένω.d: I remain, abide, stay, wait; with acc: I wait for, await.

μέσος.d: middle, in the middle, between, in the midst of.

μέτρον.d: a measure, whether lineal or cubic; a measuring rod.

μέχρι(ς).d: as far as, until, even to.

μήποτε.g: lest at any time, lest, perhaps
μήποτε.d: lest at any time, lest; then weakened: whether perhaps, whether at all; in a principal clause: perhaps.

μήτι.d: if not, unless, whether at all.

μίλιον.d: a Roman mile, measuring 1478.5 meters or 5820.9 feet.

μίσθιος.d: a paid worker, hired servant, hireling (contrasted with a slave).

μαίνομαι.d: I am raving mad, speak as a madman.

μαθητεύω.g: I make disciples, make into disciples
μαθητεύω.d: I make a disciple of, train in discipleship; pass: I am trained, discipled, instructed.

μακαρίζω.d: I bless, pronounce blessed or happy.

μακαρισμός.g: regarding as happy, blessed, or enviable

μακράν.d: at a distance, far away, remote, alien.

μακροθυμέω.g: I suffer long, have patience, am forbearing
μακροθυμέω.d: I suffer long, have patience, am forbearing, perseverance.

μακρός.d: long, distant, far; of long duration.

μαλακός.d: (a) soft, (b) of persons: soft, delicate, effeminate.

μανθάνω.d: I learn; with adj. or nouns: I learn to be so and so; with acc. of person who is the object of knowledge; aor. sometimes: to ascertain.

μαντεύομαι.d: I divine, practice soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.

μαραίνομαι.d: pass: I die, wither (like the grass).

μαρτυρέω.d: I witness, bear witness, give evidence, testify, give a good report.

μαρτύρομαι.g: I call to witness, testify, solemnly charge
μαρτύρομαι.d: (properly: I call (summon) to witness, and then absolutely) I testify, protest, asseverate; I conjure, solemnly charge.

μαστιγόω.d: I flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame; met: I chastise.

ματαιόομαι.d: I become vain or foolish, am perverted.

ματαιότης.d: vanity, emptiness, unreality, purposelessness, ineffectiveness, instability, frailty; false religion.

μεγαλύνω.d: (a) I enlarge, lengthen, (b) I increase, magnify, extol.

μεγιστάν.d: a great one, a lord; a courtier, satrap, nobleman.

μεθίστημι.g: I move out of its place, transfer
μεθίστημι.d: I cause to change its place, move out of its place; I translate, transfer, remove.

μεθερμηνεύω.d: I translate (from one language into another), interpret.

μεθοδεία.d: (a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness, deceit.

μεθύσκομαι.d: I make drunk; pass: I become drunk.

μεθύω.d: I am intoxicated with wine, am drunk.

μελετάω.d: I devise, plan; practice, exercise myself in, study, ponder.

μεμβράνα.d: a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes.

μεμψίμοιρος.d: blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented, complaining.

μερίζω.d: I divide into parts, divide, part, share, distribute; mid: I share, take part in a partitioning; I distract.

μερίς.d: (a) a part, division of a country, (b) a share, portion.

μεριμνάω.d: I am over-anxious; with acc: I am anxious about, distracted; I care for.

μερισμός.d: (a) a distributing, a distribution, (b) a parting, dividing, severance, separation.

μεσίτης.d: (a) a mediator, intermediary, (b) a go-between, arbiter, agent of something good.

μεσημβρία.d: (lit: midday, hence, the position of the sun at midday), the South.

μεσονύκτιον.d: midnight, the middle of the period between sunset and sunrise.

μεσουράνημα.d: mid-heaven, the middle of heaven, the zenith.

μεσότοιχον.d: a middle wall, partition wall, barrier.

μεσόω.d: I am in the middle, am advanced midway.

μετά.d: (a) gen: with, in company with, (b) acc: (1) behind, beyond, after, of place, (2) after, of time, with nouns, neut. of adjectives.

μετάγω.g: I turn about, change the position of
μετάγω.d: (usually: transfer, transport, and met: to a better mind), I turn about, change the position of; pass: I am brought back.

μετάνοια.d: repentance, a change of mind, change in the inner man.

μετέχω.d: I have a share of, participate in, share, partake of, am a member of.
